artifacts.summary: Reproduced the Case 1 releaser race live under induced CPU load, root-caused it to a fixed-delay backgrounded releaser racing the foreground acquire-retry call's own scheduling latency, and validated a signal-file-gated fix (reusing the existing PATH-shimmed bare-sleep seam) that passed 14/14 cases at loads meeting/exceeding the reported reproduction range while the unpatched original failed reliably at the same loads.

memory_candidates.content: Shell-test fixture races between a backgrounded helper and a foreground call (neither side's assertion reading elapsed wall-clock time) are a distinct sub-shape from the elapsed-time-assertion timing axis already documented in shell-script-testing.md. Fix pattern: if the foreground function calls a bare (unqualified) command like `sleep` internally at a point that proves a precondition has already been observed (e.g. immediately after detecting contention, before backing off), PATH-shim that bare command for just the foreground invocation to touch a signal/marker file, then perform a REAL delegate call (not a faked instant return) so there is still a real window for concurrent work. Have the backgrounded helper poll for the marker's existence instead of sleeping a fixed duration before acting. This removes the race by construction instead of widening a wall-clock margin, which only raises the load threshold at which the race reappears.
